title: The overview effect
hook: Many astronauts say seeing Earth from space changed how they think about home.
peek: Many astronauts describe a sudden shift on seeing Earth hanging in space: borders vanish, the atmosphere looks paper thin, and home feels fragile. A writer popularised the name, the overview effect, in a 1987 book.
lede: Astronauts often come back describing something the training did not cover. Seeing the whole planet hanging in black space, with no borders visible and an atmosphere that looks thin as a skin, many report a lasting sense that Earth is small, fragile and shared. The writer Frank White named it, and made the name famous with his 1987 book The Overview Effect.

bullets.text: White has said the idea came to him on a cross-country flight, looking down and imagining how much stronger the view would be from space. He then interviewed astronauts about what they had felt.
Returning from the Moon on Apollo 14 in 1971, Mitchell described an overwhelming sense of connection as he watched Earth through the window. He later founded an institute to study consciousness.
Many astronauts say the atmosphere surprised them most. Seen edge-on, it looks like a thin band of blue around the planet, the layer that holds all the air anyone has ever breathed.

Researchers have interviewed astronauts and found the shift is commonly reported and sometimes long-lasting, though it is hard to measure and not everyone feels it. Some groups now try to recreate a taste of it with virtual reality.
